In the context of the Danish healthcare system, the term **Standard** refers to the specific clinical quality targets established for the diagnosis, treatment, and monitoring of patients with [[atrieflimren]] (atrial fibrillation). These benchmarks are defined and tracked by the [[Databasen for Atrieflimren i Danmark]] (AFDK) under the umbrella of the [[Regionernes Kliniske Kvalitetsudviklingsprogram]] (RKKP) [^src1], [^src12]. The [[afdk-styregruppe]] (AFDK Steering Committee) is responsible for setting these standards, which serve as the definitive measures of good clinical practice and healthcare quality across Danish hospitals [^src4], [^src5].

The standards are distributed across eight primary clinical indicators ([[Indikator]]), each targeting a specific phase of patient care. For initial diagnosis and treatment, [[Indikator 1]] measures the wait time for [[antikoagulationsbehandling]] (anticoagulation treatment), requiring that ≥ 90% of eligible patients begin treatment within 30 days of their diagnosis [^src1], [^src12]. The steering committee explicitly considers this 90% target fulfillment to be the baseline for good clinical practice [^src4], [^src5], [^src18]. Similarly, [[Indikator 2]] mandates that ≥ 80% of newly diagnosed patients undergo [[Ekkokardiografi]] (echocardiography) within a defined window around their diagnosis [^src1], [^src6], [^src11], [^src12], while [[Indikator 3]] requires that ≥ 95% of patients have their [[thyreoideastimulerende hormon (TSH)]] levels measured to rule out underlying thyroid dysfunction [^src1], [^src6], [^src12], [^src13].

Long-term management and monitoring are governed by strict adherence standards. [[Indikator 4a]]—which is subdivided into [[Indikator 4a1]], [[Indikator 4a2]], and [[Indikator 4a3]]—tracks the continuation of [[antikoagulationsbehandling]] at 1, 2, and 5 years post-diagnosis, setting a uniform standard of ≥ 90% for each interval [^src1], [^src2], [^src7], [^src12], [^src14], [^src17]. For patients specifically prescribed [[DOAC]] (Direct Oral Anticoagulants), [[Indikator 4b]] requires a ≥ 95% compliance rate for annual [[S-creatinin]] blood tests to monitor kidney function [^src1], [^src8], [^src12]. 

The database also tracks severe clinical outcomes, though the standards here are framed as maximum acceptable incidence rates rather than minimum compliance targets. [[Indikator 5]] sets a strict ceiling for the incidence of [[Iskæmisk apopleksi]] (ischemic stroke) at ≤ 0.8% (or ≤ 0.8 per 100 risk years) among prevalent patients [^src1], [^src3], [^src9], [^src12]. [[Indikator 6]] caps the incidence of [[Intrakraniel blødning]] (intracranial bleeding) at ≤ 0.6% [^src1], [^src12]. Notably, while [[Indikator 7]] tracks the incidence of major bleeding using criteria from the [[International Society of Thrombosis and Hemostasis]] (ISTH), the steering committee has deliberately chosen not to set a numerical standard for this specific metric [^src1], [^src12]. Finally, addressing patient empowerment, [[Indikator 8]] requires that ≥ 50% of newly diagnosed patients are offered a [[Struktureret undervisningsprogram]] (structured education program) within their first year of diagnosis [^src1], [^src10], [^src12], [^src15], [^src16].
